chapter: Rhythm Club, studio dates and the 1930s big bands
title: Recording with Benny Morton and Jerry Blake
summary: Welburn lists McRae's early 1934 sessions with Benny Morton and asks about Jerry Blake, who McRae knew from hotel gigs.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: You made some recordings at that time -- they were some of your first recordings.
Among them were -- you recorded with Benny Morton in 1934 in February. You did some things -- "Get Going", "Fare Thee Well To Harlem", "Tailor Made", "Golddigger Song?"
One of the musicians who was with you was Jerry Blake. He was a fellow reed man, wasn't he?
Let's talk about Jerry Blake. Where was he from and what kind of musician was he?
Jerry Blake was a -- Jerry worked with me a different (inaudible) -- where did he work with me?
Cut that off for a minute. I think --
Well, Jerry Blake -- after he came back from Europe, we did some recordings
